      "observations": [
        "All five owned paths and complete changed test bodies were read. getListedMessages gains an optional options object with 11 sort types and ascending/descending order. The schema says sortOrder is ignored without sortType and default sorting is descending. Documentation performance comparisons are not measurements from this study.",
        "With sortType, the mail-tab API first collects the entire current filtered view into a separate header array, calls the shared sortMessages helper and starts the list from the sorted result. It does not call a UI sort operation. Without sortType it retains the scheduled async addMessage loop and requests the next page as messages arrive. A missing dbView returns an empty list before either path.",
        "The shared helper creates cached headers and uses descending unless ascending is explicitly requested. It enriches junk, tag, author/recipient and priority sort keys as needed. Tests expect stable relative order among equal keys. This entry reuses the earlier folder-list implementation through its actual caller; it does not establish a new universal sorting convention.",
        "The new test_listed_messages_as_sorted task calls browser.messages.list(folder.id, sortOptions), not browser.mailTabs.getListedMessages. Its 24 expected arrays directly check the shared helper through the folder API. Neither this task name nor its getListedMessages completion label proves the new mail-tab options branch was exercised.",
        "The earlier renamed as-viewed task still calls mailTabs.getListedMessages without options and compares the API results with the UI after filtering and a UI sort change. The new task does not directly assert mail-tab sort overrides, preservation of displayed order after an override, sorted multi-page output, absent-view handling or sortOrder-only behavior. It uses 10 messages in one returned page.",
        "Fixture messages have explicit UTC dates, controlled header priorities and approximate relative body sizes. The test translates spam into the API junk flag and waits for read/junk/flagged/tag updates before sorting. stored_tags represents the expected key-based tag order; it is not user-applied tag sequence.",
        "The shared test head now accepts raw message strings and funnels file/string helpers through addGeneratedMessage. The changed From regular expression accepts the test bare address form as well as a display-name form; the code uses match[0] and assumes a matching header. It is a bounded fixture adapter, not a general MIME address parser.",
        "New sort assertions have non-empty should messages. The unchanged as-viewed privileged callbacks retain message-less Assert.deepEqual calls, and the previously inspected shared deep-equality helper still has its description-forwarding limit. EXPEXTED_SORTS is a local misspelled identifier, not a naming recommendation. Accepted later mail-tab changes affect other event/filter branches; the owned sorted/fast-list branch and test body remain unchanged.",
        "The complete fresh primary Bug2004030 description/comments 0–2 and real footer were read from its registered capture. It identifies prior folder-list sorting in Bug1977855 and says requested sorting cannot use fast push. That prior full Bug remains a bounded reused family locator here; no new page or wider source study is opened.",
        "The full D275241 summary, creation-to-final timeline and all four actual inline bodies were read, including the complete submitted documentation suggestion. The reviewer asks to warn about snapshot cost for large folders. The proposed replacement of the function description is not adopted verbatim: the author instead adds a relative-speed comparison to sortType, as the exact owned schema shows.",
        "The author explains that the From regex must accept both a bare address and a display-name/address form. The owned helper change matches that fixture need, while retaining its match assumption and whole-match use. It is not a claim of general MIME address parsing.",
        "The review praises the tests and contains remote build completions, but no submitted human request or approval changes the actual API invoked by the new sorting task. The direct source still calls messages.list; mail-tab override, UI invariance and sorted pagination remain unasserted. The claimed latency comparison is documentation and author/reviewer context, not a benchmark run."
      ],
